findings.description: Instances launched in this subnet are automatically assigned public IPv4 addresses. Combined with the associated default route through the Internet Gateway, this unnecessarily exposes workloads placed here to the internet.

Instances launched in this subnet are automatically assigned public IPv4 addresses. This subnet is associated with a route table that has an internet default route, expanding the internet-reachable attack surface for workloads launched here.
The EBS data volume does not set encrypted = true or a KMS key, so its contents may be stored unencrypted at rest unless account-level defaults happen to override this configuration.

The instance user-data embeds an AWS access key ID and secret access key. User data is accessible to software on the instance and can be retrieved through instance metadata by an attacker who gains code execution, exposing reusable AWS credentials.
No encrypted root_block_device configuration is specified for the instance. The root EBS volume can therefore be created without encryption unless an external account-level default overrides it.

SSH (TCP/22) is allowed from 0.0.0.0/0, permitting any internet host to attempt administrative access to the publicly addressed instance. This exposes the host to scanning, brute force, and exploitation attempts.
All outbound protocols and ports are allowed to 0.0.0.0/0. A compromised instance can use this broad egress path for unrestricted command-and-control connections or data exfiltration.

The bucket receiving VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration. Sensitive network metadata stored in the archive may therefore be unencrypted at rest unless a separate account- or organization-level policy enforces encryption.
The snapshot is created from a volume that is not configured for encryption, so the backup can contain the volume's data without encryption at rest.
